title: Present simple vs present continuous
vi: Hiện tại đơn và hiện tại tiếp diễn
rule: Use the present simple for habits, facts and states. Use the present continuous for actions happening now or around now.

wrong.text: I am understanding you now.

right.text: I understand you now.

tip: State verbs (know, like, understand, want, taste) are almost never used in the continuous.

title: Past simple vs past continuous
vi: Quá khứ đơn và quá khứ tiếp diễn
rule: Use the past simple for finished actions. Use the past continuous for a longer action in progress that was interrupted or set the scene.

wrong.text: I cooked dinner when the phone rang.

right.text: I was cooking dinner when the phone rang.

tip: The long background action takes -ing; the short action that interrupts it takes the past simple.

title: Present perfect vs past simple
vi: Hiện tại hoàn thành và quá khứ đơn
rule: Use the present perfect for experiences, unfinished periods and past actions with a result now. Use the past simple with a finished time (yesterday, in 2019, ago).

wrong.text: I have seen that film last night.

right.text: I saw that film last night.

tip: If you can say WHEN it happened (a finished time), use the past simple.

title: Future forms
vi: Các cách diễn đạt tương lai
rule: Will: predictions, promises, instant decisions. Going to: plans and predictions from evidence. Present continuous: fixed arrangements. Present simple: timetables.

wrong.text: Look at those clouds! It will rain.

right.text: Look at those clouds! It is going to rain.

tip: After time words like when, before, after and as soon as, use the present simple, not will.

title: Subject–verb agreement
vi: Sự hòa hợp chủ ngữ – động từ
rule: A singular subject takes a singular verb (works, is, has); a plural subject takes a plural verb (work, are, have). Find the real subject first.

wrong.text: This one look good. It work now.

right.text: This one looks good. It works now.

tip: This is one of your most repeated mistakes: it work → it works, this one look → this one looks.

title: Making questions
vi: Cách đặt câu hỏi
rule: Most questions need a helper verb before the subject: question word + do/does/did/is/are/have/can + subject + verb. Subject questions (Who called?) don't use do.

wrong.text: How to change the language?

right.text: How do I change the language?

tip: "How to...?" is not a full question. Say "How do I...?" or "How can I...?"

title: Negatives
vi: Câu phủ định
rule: Make negatives with a helper verb + not: don't/doesn't/didn't + base verb, isn't/aren't, haven't/hasn't. Use only one negative word per idea.

wrong.text: It still not load.

right.text: It still doesn't load.

tip: Never put "not" straight before a main verb in the present or past simple.

title: Articles: a, an, the, no article
vi: Mạo từ a, an, the, không mạo từ
rule: Use a/an for one thing mentioned for the first time (an before a vowel SOUND). Use the for something specific or unique. Use no article for general plural or uncountable ideas.

wrong.text: I want to do an master's degree.

right.text: I want to do a master's degree.

tip: It's the SOUND that matters: a university (/juː/), an hour (silent h).

title: Countable, uncountable and quantifiers
vi: Danh từ đếm được, không đếm được và từ chỉ lượng
rule: Countable nouns have plurals and use many / few / a few. Uncountable nouns have no plural and use much / little / a little. Some, any and a lot of work with both.

wrong.text: Find me some project idea.

right.text: Find me some project ideas.

tip: After "some", a countable noun must be plural.

title: Irregular plurals
vi: Danh từ số nhiều bất quy tắc
rule: Most nouns add -s or -es, but many common and academic nouns are irregular.

wrong.text: all the vertex

right.text: all the vertices

tip: Academic words from Latin and Greek often change their ending: analysis → analyses, phenomenon → phenomena.

title: Pronouns and possessives
vi: Đại từ và sở hữu
rule: its = belonging to it; it's = it is. whose = belonging to whom. Reflexives: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves.

wrong.text: We built it ourself.

right.text: We built it ourselves.

tip: Possessives never take an apostrophe: its, yours, hers, theirs.

title: Prepositions of time and place
vi: Giới từ chỉ thời gian và nơi chốn
rule: in: months, years, cities, countries. on: days, dates, surfaces. at: clock times, night, exact points. since: a starting point. for: a length of time.

wrong.text: Output the files at Documents.

right.text: Output the files to Documents.

tip: At → in → on goes from small point to bigger area/time, but dates and days always take on.

title: Comparatives and superlatives
vi: So sánh hơn và so sánh nhất
rule: Short adjectives: -er / the -est. Long adjectives: more / the most. Irregular: good → better → best, bad → worse → worst.

wrong.text: This one is more faster.

right.text: This one is faster.

tip: Never use more with an -er form.

title: Modal verbs: ability, obligation, advice
vi: Động từ khuyết thiếu: khả năng, bắt buộc, lời khuyên
rule: Modals are followed by the base verb with no "to" and never take -s: can, could, must, should, may, might. "Have to" and "need to" do take "to".

wrong.text: She cans swim. You should to go.

right.text: She can swim. You should go.

tip: mustn't = it's forbidden; don't have to = it's not necessary.

title: Gerund or infinitive
vi: Danh động từ hay động từ nguyên mẫu
rule: After prepositions and some verbs (enjoy, mind, avoid, keep, how about), use -ing. After other verbs (want, decide, promise, hope), use to + verb.

wrong.text: How about remove them? It keeps add a line.

right.text: How about removing them? It keeps adding a line.

tip: "Looking forward to" and "interested in" end in a preposition, so they take -ing.

title: Capitals and basic punctuation
vi: Viết hoa và dấu câu cơ bản
rule: Capitalise I, the first word of a sentence, names, languages, nationalities, days, months and brands. Put no space before ? or !. End every sentence with a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark.

wrong.text: what should i do now ?

right.text: What should I do now?

tip: In English the question mark touches the last word, with no space.

title: Present perfect continuous
vi: Hiện tại hoàn thành tiếp diễn
rule: Use have/has been + -ing for an activity that started in the past and is still going on, or has just stopped with a visible result. Use the simple form for finished amounts (three chapters).

wrong.text: I am learning English for five years.

right.text: I have been learning English for five years.

tip: With state verbs (know, own, believe) use the present perfect simple instead.

title: Past perfect
vi: Quá khứ hoàn thành
rule: Use had + past participle for an action that happened before another past action.

wrong.text: When I arrived, the train has left.

right.text: When I arrived, the train had left.

tip: You only need the past perfect when the order of two past events matters.

title: Conditionals: zero, first and second
vi: Câu điều kiện loại 0, 1, 2
rule: Zero: If + present, present (facts). First: If + present, will + verb (real future). Second: If + past, would + verb (unreal or imaginary now).

wrong.text: If I have one more month, I will add more data.

right.text: If I had one more month, I would add more data.

tip: Never put will or would in the if-clause.

title: Third and mixed conditionals
vi: Câu điều kiện loại 3 và hỗn hợp
rule: Third: If + had + participle, would have + participle (imagining a different past). Mixed: If + had + participle, would + verb now (past cause, present result).

wrong.text: If I had studied harder, I would pass the exam.

parts.t: If I had studied harder, I

right.text: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.

parts.t: If I had studied harder, I

tip: Use the mixed form when the result is still true now.

title: The passive voice
vi: Câu bị động
rule: be + past participle. Use it when the action matters more than who did it, or the doer is unknown. Add "by + doer" only if it's important.

formula.text: am / is / are / was / were / been

wrong.text: Why is it lock? That AI is host on Azure.

right.text: Why is it locked? That AI is hosted on Azure.

tip: The tense is shown by "be": is done, was done, has been done, will be done.

title: Relative clauses
vi: Mệnh đề quan hệ
rule: who = people, which = things, whose = possession, where = places, when = times. Non-defining clauses (with commas) use which/who, never that.

wrong.text: He was the one that interview me.

right.text: He was the one who interviewed me.

tip: If you can remove the clause and the sentence still makes sense, it's non-defining: use commas and no "that".

title: Reported speech
vi: Câu tường thuật
rule: When the reporting verb is in the past, move tenses back one step (am → was, have → had, will → would). Reported questions use normal word order.

wrong.text: She asked me where did I live.

right.text: She asked me where I lived.

tip: Say + (that); tell + person: She told me... / She said that...

title: Modals of deduction
vi: Động từ khuyết thiếu chỉ suy đoán
rule: must = I'm almost sure it's true. can't = I'm almost sure it's not true. might / may / could = it's possible. For the past, add have + participle.

wrong.text: He must not have seen it; he was abroad.

right.text: He can't have seen it; he was abroad.

tip: The opposite of "must" for deduction is "can't", not "mustn't".

title: Adjectives, adverbs and adjective order
vi: Tính từ, trạng từ và trật tự tính từ
rule: Adjectives describe nouns; adverbs (often -ly) describe verbs and adjectives. Order before a noun: opinion → size → age → shape → colour → origin → material → noun.

wrong.text: I very like going outside.

right.text: I really like going outside.

tip: "Very" can't modify a verb. Use "really" or "very much" at the end: I like it very much.

title: Linking words: contrast, reason, result, addition
vi: Từ nối: tương phản, nguyên nhân, kết quả, bổ sung
rule: although / even though / because + clause. despite / in spite of / because of / due to + noun or -ing. however / therefore / moreover start a new sentence or follow a semicolon, with a comma after.

wrong.text: Despite it was raining, we went out.

parts.t: it was raining, we went out.

right.text: Although it was raining, we went out.

parts.t: it was raining, we went out.

tip: Despite never takes a full clause directly. Use "despite the fact that" if you need one.

title: Sentence boundaries and comma splices
vi: Ranh giới câu và lỗi nối câu bằng dấu phẩy
rule: Two complete sentences can't be joined by a comma alone. Use a full stop, a semicolon, or a comma + and / but / so.

wrong.text: It looks good, help me install it.

right.text: It looks good. Help me install it.

tip: This is one of your most frequent habits. Before each comma, ask: could both sides stand alone? If yes, use a full stop.

title: Dependent prepositions
vi: Giới từ đi kèm
rule: Many adjectives, verbs and nouns are always followed by a particular preposition. Learn them as chunks: interested in, depend on, good at, related to.

wrong.text: The program is focused about research.

right.text: The program is focused on research.

tip: When you learn a new word, learn its preposition with it.

title: Used to, be used to, get used to
vi: Used to, be used to, get used to
rule: used to + verb = a past habit that is no longer true. be used to + noun/-ing = be familiar with. get used to + noun/-ing = become familiar with.

wrong.text: I am used to play football as a child.

right.text: I used to play football as a child.

tip: In questions and negatives, write "use to": Did you use to...? I didn't use to...

title: So and such, too and enough
vi: So/such, too/enough
rule: so + adjective/adverb; such (a/an) + (adjective) + noun. too + adjective = more than is good. adjective + enough / enough + noun = as much as needed.

wrong.text: It was so a good film.

right.text: It was such a good film.

tip: Enough goes AFTER an adjective (old enough) but BEFORE a noun (enough time).

title: Future perfect and future continuous
vi: Tương lai hoàn thành và tương lai tiếp diễn
rule: will have + participle = finished before a future time. will be + -ing = in progress at a future time. will have been + -ing = duration up to a future time.

wrong.text: By 2030, I will finish my master's.

right.text: By 2030, I will have finished my master's.

tip: "By + future time" is the strongest signal for the future perfect.

title: Participle clauses
vi: Mệnh đề phân từ
rule: Shorten clauses with -ing (active), -ed / past participle (passive) or having + participle (an earlier action). The subject must be the same as in the main clause.

wrong.text: Having publish in 1897, Dracula is popular.

right.text: Published in 1897, Dracula is popular.

tip: Check the hidden subject: "Walking home, the rain started" wrongly says the rain was walking.

title: Wish, if only and would rather
vi: Wish, if only và would rather
rule: wish + past = unreal now. wish + past perfect = regret about the past. wish + would = annoyance or a wish for change. would rather + base verb (me), would rather + person + past (someone else).

wrong.text: I wish I have more time.

right.text: I wish I had more time.

tip: Use "were" for every person: I wish I were taller.

title: Causatives: have / get something done
vi: Thể sai khiến: have / get something done
rule: have / get + object + past participle = someone does it for you. have + person + base verb; get + person + to + verb.

wrong.text: I had my hair cutted yesterday.

right.text: I had my hair cut yesterday.

tip: "I cut my hair" means you did it yourself; "I had my hair cut" means a hairdresser did it.

title: Emphasis, question tags and short responses
vi: Nhấn mạnh, câu hỏi đuôi và câu trả lời ngắn
rule: Use do/does/did for emphasis. Question tags repeat the helper verb with the opposite polarity. So/Neither + helper + subject agree with someone.

wrong.text: I'm right, amn't I?

right.text: I'm right, aren't I?

tip: Positive sentence → negative tag; negative sentence → positive tag.

title: Ellipsis and substitution
vi: Lược bỏ và thay thế
rule: Avoid repetition: replace a noun with one/ones, a clause with so/not, or leave out words after a helper verb (I can't, but she can).

formula.text: I can't speak French, but she can

wrong.text: "Can you lend me a pen?" "Sorry, I don't have it."

parts.t: "Can you lend me a pen?" "Sorry, I don't have

right.text: "Can you lend me a pen?" "Sorry, I don't have one."

parts.t: "Can you lend me a pen?" "Sorry, I don't have

tip: Smooth substitution makes Speaking sound fluent and natural (Band 7+ coherence).

title: Parallel structure
vi: Cấu trúc song song
rule: Items in a list or pair must have the same grammatical form: reading, writing and coding; to travel, to learn and to meet.

wrong.text: I like reading, writing and to code.

right.text: I like reading, writing and coding.

tip: Check every list in your essay: all nouns, all -ing forms, or all base verbs.

title: Advanced passive: it is said that…
vi: Bị động nâng cao: it is said that…
rule: Report general opinions without naming who holds them: It is said / believed / thought that... or Subject + is said / believed + to + verb (or to have + participle for the past).

wrong.text: People says that the castle is haunted.

right.text: It is said that the castle is haunted.

tip: Very useful in Writing Task 2 to introduce a view: It is widely believed that...

title: Inversion for emphasis
vi: Đảo ngữ để nhấn mạnh
rule: After a negative or limiting expression at the start (Never, Rarely, Not only, Hardly, Only after, Under no circumstances), put the helper verb before the subject, like a question.

wrong.text: Never I have seen such a castle.

right.text: Never have I seen such a castle.

tip: Inversion is a strong Band 8–9 feature in Writing, but use it once or twice per essay, not in every paragraph.

title: Cleft sentences
vi: Câu chẻ (nhấn mạnh)
rule: Split a sentence to focus on one part: It is/was + focus + that/who... or What + clause + is/was + focus.

wrong.text: That I need is more practice.

right.text: What I need is more practice.

tip: Clefts are useful in Speaking to sound natural and emphatic: What I really like about my city is...

title: The subjunctive and formal "that" clauses
vi: Thức giả định và mệnh đề "that" trang trọng
rule: After words like imperative, essential, vital, suggest, recommend, insist and demand + that, use the base verb for every subject (no -s, no past form).

wrong.text: It is essential that he is informed.

right.text: It is essential that he be informed.

tip: This is a strong Band 8–9 structure for Writing Task 2 recommendations.

title: Nominalisation (formal noun forms)
vi: Danh từ hóa (văn phong trang trọng)
rule: Academic writing often turns verbs and adjectives into nouns: increase → an increase, decide → a decision, important → the importance.

formula.text: There was a sharp increase in prices.

wrong.text: There has been a sharp increased in prices.

right.text: There has been a sharp increase in prices.

tip: Nominalisation helps IELTS Writing Task 1 and Task 2 sound academic, but don't overuse it.

title: Hedging (cautious academic language)
vi: Ngôn ngữ thận trọng trong văn học thuật
rule: Avoid overclaiming. Use tend to, appear to, may, might, it could be argued that, to some extent, arguably, it is likely that.

wrong.text: This proves that diet is the only cause.

parts.t: that diet is the only cause.

right.text: This suggests that diet plays a role.

tip: Examiners reward measured claims. "All", "always" and "proves" are risky in Task 2.

title: Number, amount and quantity phrases
vi: Cụm từ chỉ số lượng
rule: the number of + plural noun → singular verb. a number of + plural noun → plural verb. Half of / most of / percent of → the verb agrees with the noun after "of".

wrong.text: The number of students have increased.

right.text: The number of students has increased.

tip: This is essential for IELTS Writing Task 1 when describing data.
